mission_10: Meta-learning for NLP applies few-shot learning techniques to natural language tasks, where the challenge is compounded by the discrete, high-dimensional nature of text. Prototypical networks for text classification represent documents as mean word embeddings (from Word2Vec, GloVe, or contextual embeddings), then classify by distance to class prototypes. Prompt-based few-shot learning leverages large language models' in-context learning ability: providing a few labeled examples (demonstrations) in the prompt enables the model to perform the task without parameter updates. Cross-lingual few-shot transfer uses word translation dictionaries or shared embedding spaces to transfer classifiers trained in one language to another. Meta-learning for language model adaptation fine-tunes pre-trained models (like BERT) on few examples of a new task, using MAML-style optimization to learn an initialization that adapts quickly. These techniques are essential for low-resource NLP, where labeled data is scarce for many languages, domains, and tasks.
